Rashi on Yevamot 13a:10:1.hebrew: זו - דמתני' דהכא, דכנס ולבסוף גירש — מותרת, כדקתני: "ומתה בתו או נתגרשה". ואין צ"ל זו דג' אחים, דגירש ולבסוף כנס:
Rashi on Yevamot 13a:10:1.english: This - [This refers to] our mishna here, where he married [the co-wife] and subsequently divorced [the daughter, yet the co-wife is] permitted, as it teaches: “And [if] his daughter died or was divorced”; and “it is unnecessary to say that” [refers to] that [mishna] of three brothers, where he divorced [the first wife] and subsequently married [the second wife].

Rashi on Yevamot 13a:11:1.hebrew: ותמאן - הערוה השתא, ותאמר: "אי איפשי בקדושין שקדשוני אמי ואחי לבעלי המת", ותעקור קידושין הראשונים, ותתייבם צרתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 13a:11:1.english: And let her refuse - [Let] the forbidden relative [refuse] now, and say: "I do not want the betrothal with which my mother and my brothers betrothed me to my deceased husband," and [thereby] uproot the original betrothal, and let her rival wife enter into levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 13a:12:1.english: She can refuse his levirate betrothal - [This refers to] that which was taught later in chapter Beit Shammai: "And Beit Hillel say: [She may perform refusal] with a husband and with a yavam."

Rashi on Yevamot 13a:12:2.hebrew: למאמרו - הוא דממאנת, שאם עשה היבם מאמר ביבמה קטנה ומיאנה בו, מפקיע מיאון את המאמר, וחזרה לזיקה לבדה וחולצת. ואע"ג דגדולה שעשה בה מאמר ולא רצה לכנוס, קי"ל בפ' ר"ג (לקמן יבמות דף נ:) צריכה גט למאמרו וחליצה לזיקתו — הכא, מיאון עקר למאמרו, ולא בעיא גיטא:
Rashi on Yevamot 13a:12:2.english: To his levirate betrothal - It is [specifically] to this that she may perform refusal: that if the yavam performed a levirate betrothal [ma’amar] with a minor yevama, and she refused him, the refusal annuls the levirate betrothal, and she returns to the levirate bond alone and performs chalitzah. And even though, in the case of an adult [yevama] with whom he performed a levirate betrothal and did not wish to marry [her], we hold in the chapter 'Rabban Gamliel' (below, Yevamot 50b) that she requires a bill of divorce [get] for his levirate betrothal and chalitzah for his bond — here, refusal uproots his levirate betrothal, and she does not require a bill of divorce.

Rashi on Yevamot 13a:12:3.hebrew: ואין ממאנת לזיקתו - לעקור נשואים ראשונים, ולהפקיע זיקת ייבום, ולצאת בלא חליצה. ה"נ גבי ערוה, לא עקר ליה מיאון דהשתא לנשואין קמאי למישרי צרתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 13a:12:3.english: And she cannot refuse his bond - [So as] to uproot the first marriage, dissolve the levirate bond, and leave without ḥalitzah. So too, in the case of a forbidden relative, a refusal [performed] now does not uproot the first marriage so as to permit her rival wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 13a:13:1.hebrew: צרת ערוה שאני - רבנן גזרו שלא תמאן ליבומי צרתה, דלא לזלזולי בצרת ערוה, דלמא אתי למישרי:
Rashi on Yevamot 13a:13:1.english: The rival wife of a forbidden relative is different - The Sages decreed that she may not perform refusal [in order] to allow her rival wife to enter into levirate marriage, so as not to treat [the prohibition of] the rival wife of a forbidden relative lightly, lest one come to permit [her].

Rashi on Yevamot 13a:13:2.hebrew: מיאנה - כלתו בבעלה, מותרת לחמיה, דעקרתה לנישואיה והויא כמפותת בנו, ומותרת לו. אבל מת בנו, בעלה הראשון, ומיאנה בזיקת יבם — אע"ג דנשואין קמאי עקרה, אסורה לאביו. אלמא משעת נפילה כלתו היא. משעה שנפלה להתייבם ונזקקה ליבם מחמת נישואין הראשונים, נראים אותם נישואין גמורים למיהוי אשת המת וכלתו של זה:
Rashi on Yevamot 13a:13:2.english: She refused - [If] his daughter-in-law [refused] her husband, she is permitted to her father-in-law, for she uprooted her marriage and is like a woman seduced by his son, and is permitted to him. However, [if] his son, her first husband, died, and she refused the levirate bond — even though she uproots the first marriage, she is forbidden to his father. Evidently, from the moment of falling [to levirate marriage], she is his daughter-in-law. From the moment she fell to enter levirate marriage and became bound to the *yavam* on account of the first marriage, that marriage appears complete, so as [for her] to be the wife of the deceased and this one's daughter-in-law.

Rashi on Yevamot 13a:14:1.hebrew: ה"נ - בצרת ערוה, משעת נפילה שנזקקה הבת ליבם למאן בו, מחמת קידושי ראשון נראים נישואים גמורים למיהוי אשת המת וצרתה צרת הבת. ואי שרית ליה, אתי למישרי צרת הבת בעלמא:
Rashi on Yevamot 13a:14:1.english: Here too - In [the case of] the rival wife of a forbidden relative, from the moment of falling [before the yavam], when the daughter became bound to the yavam to perform refusal against him, on account of the first [husband's] betrothal the marriage appears [to be] a complete marriage, so that [she] is the deceased's wife and her rival wife is the daughter's rival wife. And if you were to permit her [to enter into levirate marriage], people would come to permit the rival wife of a daughter in general.

Rashi on Yevamot 13a:15:1.hebrew: שש עריות - יש שחמורות מאלו. ומהו חומר שלהן? שנשואות לאחרים, ואינן יכולין להנשא לאחיו מאביו. ואם מתו בעליהן, שהן נכריות אצל זה — צרותיהן מותרות להנשא לזה:
Rashi on Yevamot 13a:15:1.english: Six forbidden relations - There are [some] that are more severe than these. And what is their severity? That they are married to others, and they cannot be married to his paternal brother. And if their husbands died, since they are unrelated to this [man] — their rival wives are permitted to marry this [man].

Rashi on Yevamot 13a:16:1.hebrew: אמו - אינה יכולה להנשא לאחיו של זה מאביו, שהרי היא לו אשת האב. וכן אשת האב, ואחות אביו, ואשת אחיו מאביו שהיו לו בנים, ואשת אחי אביו — כולן אסורות לאחיו מאביו כשם שאסורות עליו, ואין בהן צד ייבום על זה לעולם. ואם נישאו לאחרים, ולהם נשים אחרות, ומתו — מותרות לינשא לזה, שאין צרת ערוה אסורה אלא כשנפלה לייבום עם הערוה פעם אחת, שכיון שפטרה לצרת ערוה, עמדה עולמית באיסור אשת אח שיש לה בנים:
Rashi on Yevamot 13a:16:1.english: His mother - She cannot be married to this person’s paternal brother, for to him, she is his father’s wife. And likewise, his father’s wife, his father’s sister, the wife of his paternal brother who had children, and his father’s brother’s wife — all of them are forbidden to his paternal brother just as they are forbidden to him, and there is never any aspect of levirate marriage [falling] upon this [person] regarding them. And if they married other [unrelated men], and they [those men] had other wives, and they died — [the other wives] are permitted to marry this [person], as the rival wife of a forbidden relative is forbidden only when she fell to levirate marriage together with the forbidden relative on one occasion; for once [the forbidden relative] exempted the rival wife of the forbidden relative, she [the rival wife] remained forever under the prohibition of a brother’s wife who has children.

Rashi on Yevamot 13a:17:1.hebrew: ב"ש מתירים - צרת ערוה להתייבם לאחיו, דלית להו הך דרשה דלצרור:
Rashi on Yevamot 13a:17:1.english: Beit Shammai permit - The rival wife of a forbidden relative to enter into levirate marriage with his brothers, for they do not hold this exposition of "to be a rival" [litzror].

Rashi on Yevamot 13a:8:2.hebrew: האי תנא - דמתני' סבר: מיתת הבעל מפלת נשיו לייבום. הלכך, אפי' כנס ולבסוף גירש — כיון דבשעת מיתה לאו צרת הבת היא — שריא:
Rashi on Yevamot 13a:8:2.english: This tanna - [The tanna] of our mishna maintains that the husband's death casts his wives to levirate marriage. Therefore, even [if] he married [the daughter] and ultimately divorced [her], since at the time of death she is not the rival wife of the daughter, she is permitted.

Rashi on Yevamot 13a:9:1.hebrew: ותנא - דברייתא סבר, נישואין הראשונים — שהאשה נשאת לבעלה — מפילים אותה לייבום. הלכך, משנעשית צרת ערוה שעה אחת, אסורה עולמית:
Rashi on Yevamot 13a:9:1.english: And the tanna - [The tanna] of the baraita maintains [that] the first marriage — when the woman was married to her husband — causes her to fall to levirate marriage. Therefore, once she became the rival wife of a forbidden relative for [even] one hour, she is forbidden forever.

Tosafot on Yevamot 13a:11:1.hebrew: תמאן השתא ותתייבם כו' - ואפי' לר"ג, דלית ליה מלמדין את הקטנה שתמאן לקמן בפ' ב"ש (יבמות דף קט.) — היינו להוציאה מבעלה. א"נ, פריך: דהיכא דמיאנה תתייבם צרתה, ומתני' משמע דאין לה תקנה אלא בחליצה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 13a:11:1.english: "Let her perform refusal now, and let [her rival wife] enter into levirate marriage, etc." - And even according to Rabban Gamliel, who does not hold that we instruct a minor to perform refusal, later in chapter Beit Shammai (Yevamot 109a) — that is [only] to remove her from her husband. Alternatively, [the Gemara] is asking: In a case where she performed refusal, let her rival wife enter into levirate marriage; yet the Mishnah implies that she has no remedy other than ḥalitza.

Tosafot on Yevamot 13a:13:1.hebrew: לא צרת ערוה שאני כו' - ה"נ בשעת נפילה נראית כצרת בתו. וא"ת: ומנא ליה דטעמא דרמי בר יחזקאל משום דבשעת נפילה נראית ככלתו — דלמא טעמא דרמי בר יחזקאל גופיה משום דרבי אושעיא, דאינה ממאנת לזיקתו? וי"ל: דע"כ טעמא דרמי בר יחזקאל משום דבשעת נפילה נראית ככלתו, מדנקט "אסורה לאביו", מכלל דלעלמא שריא; ואי טעמא משום דאינה ממאנת לזיקתו, אסורה נמי לעלמא. וא"ת: א"כ, תקשה ברייתא דרמי בר יחזקאל לר' אושעיא? ותירץ הר"ר משה כהן: דאיכא למימר דמיירי כשחלצה, ולהכי שריא לעלמא, ולא משום דממאנת לזיקתו; א"נ, כשמיאנה ביבם אחר שנתייבמה, דליכא זיקה, ומ"מ אסורה לאביו משום דבשעת נפילה נראית ככלתו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 13a:13:1.english: "No, the rival wife of a forbidden relative is different, etc." - Here too, at the time of falling [into the levirate bond], she appeared like his daughter's rival wife. And if you say: From where does [the Gemara] know that the reason of Rami bar Yeḥezkel is that at the time of falling she appeared like his daughter-in-law — perhaps the reason of Rami bar Yeḥezkel himself is because of [the principle of] Rabbi Oshaya, that she cannot refuse his bond? And one can say: Perforce, the reason of Rami bar Yeḥezkel is that at the time of falling she appeared like his daughter-in-law, since he taught: "She is forbidden to his father," which implies that to the rest of the world she is permitted; and if the reason were that she cannot refuse his bond, she would be forbidden to the rest of the world as well. And if you say: If so, let the baraita of Rami bar Yeḥezkel pose a difficulty to Rabbi Oshaya? And Rabbi Moshe Cohen answered: It can be said that [the baraita] is dealing with [a case] where she performed ḥalitza, and for that reason she is permitted to the rest of the world, and not because she [can] refuse his bond. Alternatively, [it is dealing with a case] where she refused the yavam after she entered into levirate marriage [with him], where there is no [levirate] bond; and nevertheless, she is forbidden to his father because at the time of falling she appeared like his daughter-in-law.

Tosafot on Yevamot 13a:9:1.hebrew: נשואין הראשונים מפילים - הכא לא הוה שייך למינקט הראשונים, דליכא הכא תרי נישואין. ומשום ההיא דבפרק ב"ש (לקמן יבמות קח:) נקט הכי, דתנן: "המגרש האשה והחזירה מותרת ליבם, ור"א אוסר". ומפרש התם: טעמא דר"א משום דמספקא ליה אי מיתה מפלת, אי נישואים הראשונים מפילים:
Tosafot on Yevamot 13a:9:1.english: "The first marriage causes [her] to fall" - Here, it was not applicable to use [the term] "the first," as there are not two marriages here. And on account of that [mishnah] in the chapter "Beit Shammai" (below, Yevamot 108b), it used this [formulation]: as we learned [in a mishnah], "One who divorces [his] wife and remarries her, she is permitted to the levir, and Rabbi Eliezer forbids [her]." And [the Gemara] explains there: The reason of Rabbi Eliezer is because he is in doubt whether death causes [her] to fall [for levirate marriage] or the first marriage causes [her] to fall.
